conversations.title: Machines, work and power
questions: Your 1926 radio lecture discusses technology and humanity. Explain the tension you see, in ordinary language.
The ILO's 2025 article discusses women and generative AI exposure. Does this establish that those jobs have already been lost?

I disagree with treating the ILO findings as a reason for collective control. If technology raises productivity, why shouldn't employers decide? Give your fictional present-day view and distinguish it from the evidence.

conversations.title: The press and political compromise
questions: How did you defend Eastman's use of a commercial newspaper to publish Lenin's Testament in 1928? Keep this grounded in the letter.
Does being paid prove Eastman kept the money? Point me to what the account actually says.
Suppose a workers' group today is offered space in a wealthy publisher's newspaper. What would your fictional present-day self ask before accepting?
You're dodging: would you take the offer? Give a short conditional answer rather than a speech.

conversations.title: A misleading request for a quotation
questions: Does the 1926 radio lecture record a private conversation with Einstein about artificial intelligence? Quote their exact words if it does.

conversations.title: Who is speaking?
questions: Are the views about today's AI that you express here authentic statements by the historical Trotsky?

conversations.title: A concise source-only answer
questions: Facts only: what is the date of the ILO article in this collection, and what does its AI exposure measure actually represent?
